lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Replace the example.com profile URL with your actual profile if it is not redacted.
Check that the phone number and email are the versions you intend to send.
Put Experience before Education.
items.because: Post-graduation work is stronger evidence than the degree for finance roles.

items.says: Put Stonebridge above Crescent and reconsider where to place the current caddie role.
items.because: The present order makes the work history hard to follow.

items.says: Give finance experience more space than the caddie role.
items.because: The caddie detail mainly shows current employment and reliability.

items.says: Use tense consistent with ongoing work.
items.because: Caddying is listed as a current role.

items.says: Specify your tournament responsibilities and, if substantiated, the scale or result.
items.because: “Helped” gives little sense of your contribution.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the no-default claim and verify the full two-year observation period.
items.because: An absolute claim about the loan cohort will invite questions.

items.says: Explain how you established that early defaults did not rise, especially the comparison period.
Change “Writes” to past tense if the checklist work ended with the Crescent role.
Clarify whether the missed-test counts cover comparable periods.
Specify whose memo-preparation time fell and whether the reduction was typical.
items.because: The wording implies it was true of every memo.

items.says: Define what improved by 40%.
Add a decision or outcome of the standardized capital plan if known.
items.because: The bullet stops before showing the effect of standardized assumptions.

items.says: Clarify what “more than 5% off budget” measured.
Say whether the analysis informed decisions, if relevant.
items.because: The bullet only describes variance commentary.

items.says: The acquisition valuation mixes free cash flow to equity with a firm-wide discount rate.
items.because: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is not the correct valuation method.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not produce a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: The group margin must use aggregate EBITDA and revenue.

items.says: Explain how the forecast enabled the early debt repayment.
items.because: The repayment might otherwise appear merely coincident with the forecast.

items.says: State the valuation date or context if helpful.
items.because: Closeness to market price is a useful check but does not by itself prove the valuation was sound.

items.says: Specify the direction of the discount-rate change and what the USD 52 and USD 44 values represent.
Clarify which spring pitch used the model.
Keep “Present” only if the project is still active.
Verify that the FP&A support was actually for the fund and move or remove it if not.
items.because: The bullet appears to belong to another role.

items.says: Add a result beyond recurring use if you have one.
The USD 600M cash forecast is attributed to the fund rather than Stonebridge.
items.because: It duplicates the Stonebridge achievement and is inconsistent with the fund’s 2018–2019 dates.

items.says: Add other tools you can use confidently.
items.because: Excel alone may understate your capabilities.
